headline: Michigan State Park Pass and Wilderness Cabin Bookings
reservation: A Recreation Passport is required for all vehicle entry to the state park. While day-use areas are generally accessible, the park's popular rustic cabins and yurts require reservations months in advance through the Michigan DNR system. Changing availability for backcountry sites necessitates checking the official reservation portal before arrival.

days.title: The High Ridges and Ancient Lakes

stops.name: Lake of the Clouds Overlook
stops.detail: View the park's most famous vista where the escarpment towers over the Carp River valley.

stops.name: Escarpment Trail
stops.detail: Hike the rocky ridge for panoramic views of old-growth forest and the inland lake system.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes; roads are paved but steep near the overlooks.
days.note: Early morning often brings valley fog which may obscure views until mid-morning.

days.title: River Gorges and Lake Superior Shore

stops.name: Presque Isle River Waterfalls
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalks to see Manabezho and Manido falls carving through the bedrock.

stops.name: Presque Isle Peninsula
stops.detail: Witness the dramatic confluence where the amber river water meets the blue of Lake Superior.

days.driving: Allow 75 minutes; the drive from the east entrance to the west side is substantial.
days.note: Currents at the river mouth are hazardous; remain on designated viewing platforms.

days.title: Summits and Old Growth Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from the Visitor Center

stops.name: Summit Peak Tower
stops.detail: Climb the observation tower at the park's highest point for views extending to the Apostle Islands.

stops.name: Union Bay
stops.detail: Beachcomb for agates along the volcanic pebble shore of the world's largest freshwater lake.

days.driving: Allow 50 minutes; interior roads are narrow and require slow transit.
days.note: Biting flies are prevalent in early summer; local seasonal conditions vary by year.

intel.title: Overlook Constraints
intel.text: Lake of the Clouds parking is popular; midday arrivals may find the primary lot full during autumn color peaks. Alternative parking is available at the trailhead lower down the road.

intel.title: Wilderness Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect no cellular coverage throughout the park interior and along the river trails. Emergency phones are located at the Visitor Center and Presque Isle ranger station.

intel.title: Last Service Points
intel.text: Silver City and White Pine are the final locations for fuel before entering the park's main loop. No gas is available within the 60,000-acre wilderness boundary.

intel.title: Fall Foliage Peak
intel.text: Color changes typically peak in late September or early October, bringing the highest visitor volume. Suggested viewing times for the escarpment are before 10 AM to avoid crowds.

intel.title: Road Seasonality
intel.text: 107th Engineers Memorial Highway to the overlook is typically closed in winter. Check Michigan DOT for seasonal opening dates, usually by late May.

plan.arrival: Fly into CMX and drive west to Ontonagon for supplies and the required Recreation Passport before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for main roads; larger RVs should use caution on the winding South Boundary Road.
plan.goldenHour: Lake of the Clouds for sunset, typically best in October for vibrant foliage contrasts.
